title: OODA Loop
description: Interactive simulation of the OODA Loop (Observe, Orient, Decide, Act) decision-making cycle. Demonstrates how speed through the decision cycle provides competitive advantage in strategic situations.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Decision Making
Strategy
OODA Loop
Military Science
Business Strategy
Competitive Advantage
Agility
learningObjectives: Identify the four phases of Boyd's OODA loop in order: Observe, Orient, Decide, and Act
Explain why Boyd considered Orient the most important phase, since it filters observations through prior experience and mental models
Predict which agent accumulates more completed cycles when the Blue and Red speed sliders are set to different values between 0.2 and 3.0
Analyze how a faster agent gets inside a slower opponent's decision cycle, forcing the opponent to act on outdated observations
Evaluate how the speed-over-power principle transfers from military strategy to business, cybersecurity, and competitive sports
